approach.method_basis: The Parent walks from one scored molecule by sampling local graph edits, including direct exchanges of an aromatic nitrogen and a carbon within the same six-member ring. It normalizes molecular identities, rejects duplicates and submits the first full batch permitted by short-term inverse-motif memory. It then moves to the highest-scoring accepted neighbor even after a loss, while keeping a separate best archive. Memory records signed changes in rooted one-bond environments, keeps up to four inverse attributes from each selected transition, and vetoes a proposal when both signs match one live transition. These environments record atom properties and bond order but omit whether a bond belongs to a ring.
approach.novelty: Make inverse memory distinguish cyclic and acyclic versions of the same local environment by adding a binary ring-membership flag to every bond in its rooted motif. Ring and chain occurrences will then receive separate signed counts and restriction keys. The original motif description remains the ordering prefix, so the addition preserves priority between existing motif families. Earlier memory siblings changed sign coverage, score-based credit, count-based ranking, overlap retention or occurrence boundaries; they retained the same pooled structural descriptions. This experiment changes the topological context of the remembered attribute. It keeps the Parent's graph generation and nitrogen relocation mechanism.

hypothesis: Refine each rooted radius-one motif with binary cycle membership of its root-to-neighbor bonds, so signed occurrence counts and inverse tabu restrictions distinguish cyclic from acyclic instances of an otherwise identical local environment.

finding_summary.headline: Separating ring and chain motifs changed 20 evaluated neighbors, but all three seeds lost score
finding_summary.insights: The result rules out lack of structural activation or lack of evaluated exposure as the explanation for the missing score benefit. The original labels really did pool ring and chain occurrences, and the refined labels still transferred restrictions between distinct molecules during a live memory window. That additional topological distinction alone did not improve this search. It also did more than remove vetoes: resolving opposite changes that previously canceled changed which motif families were retained in nine transitions and created one extra veto. The largely unfavorable outcomes of the newly allocated neighbors show why passive admissions cannot be treated as evidence of useful search. The full trajectories also change when a batch stops on a different draw, so the large final losses do not identify the causal score contribution of any single annotation or unscored alternative. The supplied molecular assessment still finds aromatic and carbonyl arrangements alongside reactive heteroatom bonds, unusual sulfur cages and undefined stereochemistry. Binary cycle membership does not describe ring size, geometry, strain or chemical stability; those limitations remain open after this experiment.
finding_summary.results: The observed graphs contained 834 old motif families with multiple cycle contexts, and those distinctions reached live restrictions and scored proposals. A separate unannotated memory replay on the same sources and accepted history shows that 19 evaluated molecules were newly admitted and one evaluated molecule replaced a newly vetoed ring opening, changing 20 of 435 actual batches. Only one of these 20 molecules improved its source, by 0.001295; 19 worsened it and none tied. None immediately improved the best archive. One worsening ring closure became the next walk state, but its 20 later evaluated descendants added no archive gain. The three-seed mean final score fell from 0.521759 to 0.476854, a paired loss of 0.044906 instead of the required gain of 0.002. All three seeds declined. DRD2 and sitagliptin accounted for the largest task losses; zaleplon improved slightly on average.

molecular.headline: Aromatic carbonyl scaffolds persist, but high scores also accompany reactive decorations, sulfur cages and undefined stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: Node n-9dc03aaf234b produces medium-sized to large, heavily branched ring systems: recognizable indole/benzofuran/benzothiophene carbonyl compounds, decorated nitrogen heterocycles, aryl-linked cyclic amines, bridged amides and sulfur-dense cages. All five tasks are covered. Each digest contains 900 evaluated molecules, including 870 optimizer proposals, across seeds 0, 1 and 2. Every proposal set has ring_closure_rate 1.0 and branch_rate 1.0. Aromatic-token presence is 0.9057, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0 and 0.7264 in the supplied task order; these are fractions of strings containing aromatic tokens, not aromatic-atom fractions or evidence that every leading molecule is aromatic. Every set has charged_rate 0.0 and stereocentre_rate 0.0. Neutral SMILES can contain basic amines, and these records do not reveal protonation or stereochemical processing inside an evaluator. There is meaningful variation between seeds and tasks, but high-scoring excerpts commonly comprise close relatives of a few frameworks. An ordinary indole carboxamide is reasonably recognizable synthetic chemistry; many other leaders combine unusual sulfur coordination, heteroatom-halogen bonds or tightly connected bridges whose makeability is questionable. These coexist with useful-looking aromatic and carbonyl arrangements. The chemistry remains broadly similar to Parent n-abcd951ab7cc even where particular structures and recorded scores differ. All supplied child and parent trajectories were read passively. Structural sizes below are atom counts derived from their saved SMILES; scores are copied from those trajectories or the digest. The audit at .slots/SPIRAL2.r0011-04-improve-L16.molecular-audit.json records input hashes, graph readings and exact digest-to-trajectory matches. The digest final_molecules entries are the last evaluated neighbors of seed 2, not the best archive or all seeds combined. Missing features below distinguish absent chemical quality from demonstrated score requirements: these data cannot identify an unseen target pharmacophore, prove synthesis or establish biological activity.

method_name: Tabu search: de novo graph walks with expiring structural prohibitions
method_thesis: The anchor is the basic tabu-search procedure in Section 2 of [Glover, Tabu Search—Part I](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf), fixed before locating this external source. It chooses the best available admissible move, including a worsening move, while temporarily prohibiting reversals through short-term attribute memory. My molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation and maintains one current molecular graph, its true score, an independent best-observed archive, and expiring structural restrictions. At each feedback step, stochastically generate a new neighborhood through atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and chemically checked ring changes. Define move attributes from presence/absence changes of canonical local subgraphs around the edited region. After selecting a move, temporarily forbid a bounded record of its inverse attribute changes. These restrictions must apply to different canonical molecules sharing the affected local chemistry, so they can alter search beyond the protocol's mandatory whole-molecule duplicate rejection. Generate valid, canonical-unique, admissible neighbors until the announced batch is filled, then submit them directly without a learned score predictor. Only after real feedback choose the highest-scoring accepted neighbor as the next current graph, even when it scores below the current graph; retain the best score seen anywhere. Age restrictions by completed walk steps. If restrictions prevent sufficient fresh generation, release the oldest restrictions only as needed and record that release. This root uses the basic tabu form without an aspiration rule requiring unknown candidate scores. Preparation needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. Each objective restarts the same task-agnostic procedure with clean labeled and tabu state, and every proposed structure is generated online from the evolving current graph. The hypothesis is that an aggressive observed-neighbor choice combined with temporary structural reversal restrictions can move through useful intermediate structures and reach higher scoring molecular regions within the supplied feedback schedule. Activation requires restrictions to veto otherwise valid novel structural moves and thereby influence later current states. That diagnostic is insufficient by itself: success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Overbroad attributes may suppress productive chemistry, while overly specific attributes may never affect novel proposals; the root must expose both possibilities.

approach.method_basis: The Parent walks from one scored molecule by sampling local graph edits, including direct exchanges of an aromatic nitrogen and a carbon within the same six-member ring. It normalizes molecular identities, rejects duplicates and submits the first full batch permitted by short-term inverse-motif memory. It then moves to the highest-scoring accepted neighbor even after a loss, while keeping a separate best archive. Memory records signed changes in rooted one-bond environments, keeps up to four inverse attributes from each selected transition, and vetoes a proposal when both signs match one live transition. These environments record atom properties and bond order but omit whether a bond belongs to a ring.
approach.novelty: Make inverse memory distinguish cyclic and acyclic versions of the same local environment by adding a binary ring-membership flag to every bond in its rooted motif. Ring and chain occurrences will then receive separate signed counts and restriction keys. The original motif description remains the ordering prefix, so the addition preserves priority between existing motif families. Earlier memory siblings changed sign coverage, score-based credit, count-based ranking, overlap retention or occurrence boundaries; they retained the same pooled structural descriptions. This experiment changes the topological context of the remembered attribute. It keeps the Parent's graph generation and nitrogen relocation mechanism.

finding_summary.headline: Separating ring and chain motifs changed 20 evaluated neighbors, but all three seeds lost score
finding_summary.insights: The result rules out lack of structural activation or lack of evaluated exposure as the explanation for the missing score benefit. The original labels really did pool ring and chain occurrences, and the refined labels still transferred restrictions between distinct molecules during a live memory window. That additional topological distinction alone did not improve this search. It also did more than remove vetoes: resolving opposite changes that previously canceled changed which motif families were retained in nine transitions and created one extra veto. The largely unfavorable outcomes of the newly allocated neighbors show why passive admissions cannot be treated as evidence of useful search. The full trajectories also change when a batch stops on a different draw, so the large final losses do not identify the causal score contribution of any single annotation or unscored alternative. The supplied molecular assessment still finds aromatic and carbonyl arrangements alongside reactive heteroatom bonds, unusual sulfur cages and undefined stereochemistry. Binary cycle membership does not describe ring size, geometry, strain or chemical stability; those limitations remain open after this experiment.
finding_summary.results: The observed graphs contained 834 old motif families with multiple cycle contexts, and those distinctions reached live restrictions and scored proposals. A separate unannotated memory replay on the same sources and accepted history shows that 19 evaluated molecules were newly admitted and one evaluated molecule replaced a newly vetoed ring opening, changing 20 of 435 actual batches. Only one of these 20 molecules improved its source, by 0.001295; 19 worsened it and none tied. None immediately improved the best archive. One worsening ring closure became the next walk state, but its 20 later evaluated descendants added no archive gain. The three-seed mean final score fell from 0.521759 to 0.476854, a paired loss of 0.044906 instead of the required gain of 0.002. All three seeds declined. DRD2 and sitagliptin accounted for the largest task losses; zaleplon improved slightly on average.

applicability_conditions: The intended opportunity is the occurrence of identical existing atom/bond-order stars in different cycle contexts. If the accessible graph family has no such distinctions that reach active memory, the representation may have little or no allocation effect.

A bond's binary membership in any cycle is a topological property of the normalized sanitized molecular graph. It does not name a particular perceived ring basis, distinguish ring sizes or quantify strain; ring opening or closure can change membership along a whole affected cycle beyond the two edited endpoints.

This refined descriptor still shares attributes across different molecules with the same annotated local environment. It does not identify one physical edit site, require reversal of a whole previous molecule, encode stereochemistry or replace canonical molecular identity.

Independent comparator tables use the actual accepted history only. The registered Parent-history admissions are unscored, and the altered live walk can have different credit, overlap, validity and draw histories, including additional vetoes; the observed conditional relaxation is not a universal admissibility-superset guarantee.

The Parent includes aromatic nitrogen positional exchanges and the canonical round-trip identity repair. It does not include sibling score-gated credit, complete-signature matching, turnover ranking, independent overlap retention or count-boundary qualification, and those mechanisms are not combined here.

The mechanism operates within structural_tabu_memory on already normalized graph records, preserves direct announced-batch evaluation and all selected-feedback rules, and uses no objective identity, extra oracle labels or changed evaluation resources. Better structural discrimination does not establish improved chemical plausibility.

approach.method_basis: The Parent walks from one scored molecule by sampling local graph edits, including direct exchanges of an aromatic nitrogen and a carbon within the same six-member ring. It normalizes molecular identities, rejects duplicates and submits the first full batch permitted by short-term inverse-motif memory. It then moves to the highest-scoring accepted neighbor even after a loss, while keeping a separate best archive. Memory records signed changes in rooted one-bond environments, keeps up to four inverse attributes from each selected transition, and vetoes a proposal when both signs match one live transition. These environments record atom properties and bond order but omit whether a bond belongs to a ring.
approach.novelty: Make inverse memory distinguish cyclic and acyclic versions of the same local environment by adding a binary ring-membership flag to every bond in its rooted motif. Ring and chain occurrences will then receive separate signed counts and restriction keys. The original motif description remains the ordering prefix, so the addition preserves priority between existing motif families. Earlier memory siblings changed sign coverage, score-based credit, count-based ranking, overlap retention or occurrence boundaries; they retained the same pooled structural descriptions. This experiment changes the topological context of the remembered attribute. It keeps the Parent's graph generation and nitrogen relocation mechanism.

Their negative results rule out a generic claim that fewer vetoes, fuller signatures, positive-gain credit or more complete turnover suffices. This revisit changes that representation prerequisite while preserving their Parent's original matching, credit and lifecycle algorithms.
